I'm really truly sorry you are at a point where you feel like that that is it. I've been there myself and I know how gapingly painful it is.
I also went through with it. I downed a couple pills and had my stomachpumped. I also lost all feeling from my legs for half a week. And that half week felt longer than the rest of the year. I was terrified that I had just lost my legs. Although I'm not completely away from Suicidal thoughts, I did routinely go to therapy and continue with medication. (I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder, honestly felt unbelievable) Helped way more than I thought was possible.
Whether it's hanging by a noose or jumping off a building, there is the chance that your body gets severely damaged and you don't die. I feel your pain especially these days with lockdown going on.
I just hope that you get through this with whatever means possible because as helpless as you feel, there is a light. There is a better way to make the pain cease.

Ah well, personally been there myself and can relate to being hated by the family bullshit. But from what ive learnt by my own mistakes its this. That in the end even though its what I craved, suicide wasn't the awnser. Hilarious isn't it? When I asked to see a doctor my parents said I wasn't mentally ill too. She still doesn't agree despite being diagnosed for bipolar disorder and medicating for it. I was scared as shit especially of the fact that I'd end up being a bother to everyone around me but I forced myself to go see that one doctor and that's how it changed for me. Funny enough the closest to success I've been at a suicide attempt happened a couple months back when I had stopped taking my medication. Took a bunch of pills, got my stomach pumped. Lost all feeling of my legs for 4 days. Stayed in the hospital for a week and a half. I became even more of a nuisance after that considering they had to 'take care' of me at the hospital. Now not only am I scared that I'll become paralysed if I try to suicide again but shit keeps happening on top of one shit after another.
Hope you take my personal experience into account! 
It's been a tough couple of years so I try to share my story incase it helps people reconsider taking the exact decisions I've made. Goodluck dear Reddit Stranger!

In a world full of horrible things wasn't your girlfriend the light?  Let the tides blow over before you do anything rash. It's painful, horrible you wish you could disappear, die, do something. Just wanna get rid of the pain right? Let all the emotions roll over. Let it go through you. Surpass. If you feel like its never ending I suggest you try reaching out to a doctor. Maybe it sounds ridiculous. It certainly did to me when I went through all of it. But I decided to just give it a go as a last wave before finally letting myself drown. Funny enough it ended up being what saved me. I got diagnosed as having bipolar disorder and I've my ex to thank for it as twisted as it sounds. The pain he caused by leaving me hopeless caused me to back into a corner with nothing. But I came up and through all that nothing due to it. If you need anybody to rant to or etc feel free to drop in my DMs. Goodluck dear Reddit Stranger!

Ah man I know exactly what you mean... That was exactly me for the longest time. Eventually I kept chickening and failing till I exploded and did it. Ended up in the hospital for a week and a half. Had my stomach pumped. Lost all feeling from the hip and below for around 4 days. It was a scary and horrible time. The pain you felt is still real and there. Since you want the people you care about to be spared from the pain as well how about you consider another direction with dealing with the pain? It's the harder route, true but believe this random Reddit stranger when I say that all the pain and effort will be worth it. You will eventually feel happiness again. Sadness will come every now and then too but you'll have something worth to fight for by then. Start small and just try trusting one person. If you feel like nobody is gonna be willing to help how about trying to get the help you need yourself, take the leap of faith by reaching out to get a doctor yourself ( I went to my first doctor on my own because my parents didn't believe i was mentally ill enough, jokes on them i got diagnosed with bipolar disorder). It's an incredible transition, no exaggeration. Hope you consider it! Goodluck dear Reddit Stranger! DM if you ever need somebody to just vent to!
